Replacing a skip on the input edge with a conv gives large gains (cases 64 and 52) compared with replacing other ops.
With edge 3 absent, edge 5 is a key route to the output, so removing it cuts connectivity and costs a lot (cases 3 and 95).
Removing the input edge hurts more when edge 2 is absent because fewer alternative paths exist (cases 5, 19 and 51).
Dropping a weak avg-pool edge 1 tends to help (cases 1 and 13), unlike dropping a conv or skip there.
Replacing avg-pool with a 1x1 conv on edge 4 helps (cases 30 and 12), while it adds little when edge 4 already holds a conv or skip.
Swapping avg-pool for a skip on edge 3 gains substantially (case 24), whereas replacing a conv with a skip does not (case 84).
Replacing avg-pool on the output edge with a conv gives large gains (cases 33 and 83), while replacing a skip or conv gives small or negative changes.
With edge 0 absent, putting avg-pool on edge 1 degrades the network badly (case 79, about -19 to -22) compared with parents that keep a conv on edge 0.
When edge 3 is absent, adding a skip on edge 4 creates a new path to the output (case 65 gains +75) and is more valuable than when edge 3 already carries a path.
